criterion: The public home page runs its bands in one fixed order: a hero carrying the four-word promise over a full-bleed image, then three upcoming event cards, then a visitor invitation, then an organiser invitation with a gallery, then four blocks describing the building, then a strip of past events, then a newsletter band, then a news band above the footer.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when those eight bands appear in that order above the footer. Answer no when a band is missing or two bands appear out of that order.

criterion: The spaces page carries a drawn plan of the campus in which each hall is a separate shape labelled with its own number, the event hall is labelled XXL, and choosing a shape moves the reader to that hall's detail block below the plan.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when each hall is a distinct labelled shape and choosing one reaches that hall's detail block. Answer no when the plan is a single flat picture, when a hall carries no number, or when choosing a shape leaves the reader where they were.

criterion: Every hall detail block on the spaces page carries four labelled fields reading Capacity, Surface area, Unique features and Suitable for, and the Hall 4 block states in words that its suitability line is absent from the record.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when all four labels appear on each hall block and the Hall 4 suitability field says the line is absent. Answer no when a label is missing or the Hall 4 block carries an invented suitability sentence.

criterion: Each public route is composed for its job: the calendar sets a filter rail beside a card grid, a visit page and an about page each run as a single reading column, a legal page runs as a dated reading column stripped of decoration, and the contact page sets the enquiry form beside the practical details.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when each of those four routes uses the composition described for it. Answer no when a route borrows another one's composition, such as a legal page laid out as a card grid.

criterion: The operations console opens on a campus timeline drawing one row per space across a date axis, carrying every phase of every event, with a combination drawn across each row that combination consumes.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the timeline shows one row per space carrying build-up, run and tear-down bands. Answer no when only the run band appears, or when a combination is drawn as a single unrelated row.

criterion: The visitor map for one event draws the entrance in use, the halls that event occupies, the catering positions taken from the approved plan, the toilets and the exits, and the map still draws all of those with the network switched off.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the map renders all of those with the network off. Answer no when the page is blank, holds a loading state indefinitely, or shows an error once the network is off.

criterion: Empty, loading, refused and error read as four different answers: a list holding nothing names its one next action, a list the reader lacks the right to see says so in words, a page still loading reserves the space its rows will take, and an error is stated in words with a way forward.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when all four read differently from one another. Answer no when a refused list renders the same as an empty one, or when a list renders as blank space with no message.

criterion: The visitor and organiser reading pages lead with the practical facts: parking, routes and opening details sit within the first screen of a visit page, and the meetings, catering and restaurant pages each open with what a reader can book.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the practical facts lead each of those pages. Answer no when a decorative band pushes the practical facts below the first screen.

criterion: One strong red carries every action and every link and appears in that role alone, a deep maroon carries every line of body text, and a lighter coral appears only on hover and on a pale selection wash.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the three reds hold those three roles exclusively. Answer no when the action red appears as decoration, when body text is plain black or grey, or when the hover coral fills a resting control.

criterion: One typeface carries the whole product, depth comes from hairline rules with at most a soft shadow under a raised card, and the small status marker is the single rounded shape against corners that are barely softened elsewhere.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when one family, hairline depth and a single rounded status marker all hold. Answer no when a second display family appears, when heavy shadows carry the layout, or when buttons and cards are as rounded as the status marker.

criterion: Everything that moves shares one gesture: sections rise a short distance as each arrives and then stay put, a marker under the hero bounces to invite the first scroll, carousels slide, and the lightbox settles from slightly undersized, all at one speed on one decelerating curve.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when every moving element shares that one speed and curve. Answer no when one element moves faster or slower than the rest, or eases on a different curve.

criterion: With the device asking for reduced movement, which is the default state, the page arrives still: sections appear in place, the hero marker rests, carousels change slides at once, and a progress bar appears already at its value.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when nothing animates in that state and every change is instantaneous. Answer no when any reveal, bounce or slide still runs, or when an animation is merely shortened.

criterion: The campus plan is operable from the keyboard alone: each hall shape takes focus in a stated order with a visible outline, and focusing one announces that hall's name together with how many people the hall holds and how large the hall is.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when every hall shape is reachable by keyboard and announces name, capacity and area. Answer no when the plan cannot take focus at all, or when a focused shape announces only a number.

criterion: Meaning in this product is carried by words beside colour: an occupancy level, an event status and an unavailable control each carry a word naming that state, and the focus indicator stays visible against every surface the indicator lands on.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when each of those carries a word beside its colour and the focus indicator is visible everywhere. Answer no when a state is distinguishable only by hue, or when focus disappears on any surface.

criterion: At phone width the public site holds together in the wordiest of its three languages: navigation labels, status chips and buttons stay on one line or wrap at a word boundary, the plan becomes something the reader can pan and pinch, and calendar filters fold into a sheet above stacked cards.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when all of that holds at phone width in the longest language. Answer no when a label truncates, a chip wraps mid-word, or the page scrolls sideways.

criterion: The three surfaces used on the floor, access control, the safety board and incident raising, work on a phone held in one hand: their controls are large, sit within reach of a thumb, and stay legible under bright light.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when those three surfaces are usable one-handed at phone width with large controls. Answer no when any of the three is unusable at phone width or its controls are as small as a desktop row.
